correctness.rationale: Any maximal shortest path in K_m square K_n is a three-cell induced length-2 L path: the diameter is two and each edge extends to a distance-2 pair since m,n>=2. Hence vertex-disjoint packings have at most floor(mn/3) paths. Independently validated every digit occurs exactly three times in six RESULT templates and its cells form two adjacent sides of an L. Width-3 strips are tiled by height-2 or height-3 bricks for all m>=2. Width-2/4 strips are tiled by height 3 and remainder height 2/4 to achieve floor(2m/3)/floor(4m/3). Partition n into width-3 strips plus a width-2 or width-4 remainder, producing floor(mn/3) paths with O(mn) emitted cells. This is an all-integer constructive argument, not extrapolation from checked boards.

originality.rationale: Manuel-Brešar-Klavžar 2023 introduce maximal-geodesic packing and bound square rook graph gpack<=n²/3; their arXiv full primary paper and specific square graph lemma/nearby theorem were read, and a universal rectangular equality is not therein. Kaneko-Kelmans-Nishimura path packing allows arbitrary 3-vertex paths, unlike maximal geodesics that must be L triples; a generic nearly spanning path-packing result does not imply rook induced-L packing. Resultary geodesic results address other invariants and graph families. The optimal six-brick construction appears separate.
